root_cause.text: The Thunderbolt XDomain request handler (`tb_xdp_handle_request()` in `drivers/thunderbolt/xdomain.c`) trusted the packet after only a generic header-length check and then cast the kmemdup’d buffer to protocol-specific structs without verifying the buffer was large enough, leading to out-of-bounds reads on short packets.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `pkg_len` to `xdomain_request_work`, stores the allocated packet size in `tb_xdp_schedule_request()`, and then guards each cast with checks like `pkg_len >= sizeof(struct tb_xdp_properties)` and `pkg_len >= sizeof(struct tb_xdp_link_state_change)`, matching the CVE description that a minimal XDomain packet could pass the generic header check but still be shorter than the accessed struct.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add package length storage to xdomain request work items.
intent_record.what: A new field, `size_t pkg_len;`, was added to the `struct xdomain_request_work` definition alongside the existing `work`, `pkg`, and `tb` members.
intent_record.how: This change allows each queued xdomain request work item to carry the length of its associated package buffer, enabling later code to know how much data the request contains when processing the work.

intent_record.intent_summary: Store the request packet length in a local variable for use in request handling.
intent_record.what: A new local variable `size_t pkg_len = xw->pkg_len;` was added in `tb_xdp_handle_request()` alongside the existing `pkg` and `xhdr` pointers.
intent_record.how: This change makes the request packet length available as a local value within the function, likely for subsequent validation or parsing logic, but by itself does not alter runtime behavior in the shown hunk.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a packet length check before handling XDomain properties requests to prevent malformed short packets from being parsed.
intent_record.what: In tb_xdp_handle_request(), the PROPERTIES_REQUEST case changed the condition guarding tb_xdp_properties_response() from `if (xd)` to `if (xd && pkg_len >= sizeof(struct tb_xdp_properties))`, adding a length check before casting `pkg` to `struct tb_xdp_properties *` and using it.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now only processes a properties request when the received packet is large enough to contain a full tb_xdp_properties structure, preventing the handler from reading past the end of a short or malformed packet and avoiding invalid memory access.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a length check to ensure XDomain link state change requests are only parsed when the packet is large enough.
intent_record.what: The condition in tb_xdp_handle_request() was extended to require pkg_len to be at least sizeof(struct tb_xdp_link_state_change) before casting pkg to a tb_xdp_link_state_change pointer and using it.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now avoids treating undersized request packets as link state change messages, preventing invalid parsing of short buffers and reducing the risk of out-of-bounds access when handling XDomain link state change requests.

intent_record.intent_summary: Save the request length in the queued XDP work item so it is processed with the correct packet size.
intent_record.what: In `tb_xdp_schedule_request()`, a new assignment `xw->pkg_len = size;` was added after the allocation/error check and before `xw->tb = tb_domain_get(tb);`.
intent_record.how: This stores the packet/request length into the `xw` work item before it is queued, so the later work handler can use the correct size information at runtime. Without this assignment, the work item would carry an uninitialized or stale length value.
